nature: static repository evidence and isolated tests; no operational verification

requirements.description: Define one primary authority for track grants and its relationship to users, sessions, and static role permissions.
requirements.decision_owner: Project owner and designated IAM authority
requirements.blocker: No operational source or schema for track grants has been approved.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: A signed decision identifies the primary grant authority, grant lifecycle, audit owner, and non-contradictory relationship to existing IAM.
requirements.next_action: Obtain owner and IAM authority decision before any operational grant implementation.

requirements.description: Name who may grant, change, delegate, revoke, recover, and audit track-scoped editorial access.
requirements.blocker: Human approvers and separation-of-duties rules are not named.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Grant, delegation, emergency denial, recovery, and audit responsibilities are assigned with anti-escalation rules.
requirements.next_action: Approve a responsibility matrix; do not infer grant powers from admin/editor role names.

requirements.description: Decide whether administrative global editorial scope exists and how it is provisioned and revoked.
requirements.blocker: No operational global-scope grant or recovery policy exists in the inspected code.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Global scope is explicit, separately provisioned, independently revocable, audited, and cannot be self-granted.
requirements.next_action: Approve explicit-scope alternative or reject global scope.

requirements.description: Specify ordering for grant, role, global permission policy, session, account disablement, and global administrative scope revocations.
requirements.blocker: The static Python permission matrix has no persistent epoch participating in editorial commit; real transaction topology is not established.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Each revocable state has an explicit ordering mechanism, or the product accepts and documents a weaker revocation guarantee.
requirements.next_action: Decide policy epoch or release-drain semantics for code-defined global permissions.

requirements.description: Prove that user, session, and grant state can participate in the same confirmation boundary as editorial CAS, audit, history, and receipt.
requirements.decision_owner: Project owner, IAM authority, and operations owner
requirements.blocker: C11/C12 used synthetic records; deployed SHA, database roles, schema, and transaction topology are not verified (ADR-008 blocked).
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Authorized baseline evidence and a persistent transaction test demonstrate the selected revocation ordering on the compatible target topology.
requirements.next_action: Use the separately authorized ADR-008 evidence process; do not access infrastructure from C14.

requirements.description: Keep authentication, session validity, role permission, resource grant, capability, fence, and idempotency as distinct checks.
requirements.blocker: Operational integration is absent and not authorized.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Contract tests prove fail-closed authorization, server-issued scoped capability, and no use of fence or idempotency key as IAM.
requirements.next_action: Retain the isolated contract; require new authorization for runtime integration.

requirements.description: Use one editorial revision authority with CAS, fencing, mandatory audit, idempotency, and reconciliation semantics.
requirements.decision_owner: Project owner for product semantics; architecture owner for contract conformity
requirements.blocker: The validated contract is not integrated with active writers or the operational baseline.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Conformance tests cover stale revision/fence, atomic audit, replay, and ambiguous-result reconciliation on the approved target.
requirements.next_action: Do not create a second authority; revalidate only against the future approved baseline.

requirements.description: Revalidate all 17 C13 repository writer entries and preserve their runtime-unverified status.
requirements.blocker: Static symbol/evidence checks do not establish deployment, external tooling, or dynamic call coverage.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: All 17 IDs, symbols, source files, evidence ranges, classes, and NOT_VERIFIED runtime labels pass the offline inventory contract.
requirements.next_action: Reconcile repository inventory against an authorized runtime and operator inventory before selecting a write scope.

requirements.description: Coordinate or block every writer that can mutate the same content_blocks scope before block editing is integrated.
requirements.blocker: CRUD, publish, import, restore, duplicate, delete, seed, and administrative paths overlap; runtime invocation and containment are not verified.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Each same-scope writer is protocol-conformant, operationally disabled, or technically unable to target the pilot scope; tests prove no bypass.
requirements.next_action: Perform scope-specific call-site and operator reconciliation after baseline authorization.

requirements.description: Approve the HTTP revision, idempotency, null/absence, error, replay, and compatibility contract.
requirements.blocker: The active endpoint returns a block while the experiment uses revision/receipt semantics; old clients do not provide the proposed preconditions.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Versioning or compatibility window and fail-closed behavior for legacy clients are approved and tested.
requirements.next_action: Record API versioning, If-Match/revision, Idempotency-Key, and conflict/replay semantics.

requirements.description: Approve ACL, minimization, retention, deletion, and key lifecycle rules for audit, history, receipts, and fingerprints.
requirements.decision_owner: Product privacy owner, security owner, and project owner
requirements.blocker: ACL, retention periods, deletion exceptions, HMAC rotation, and key-loss response are not approved.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Each record class has purpose, reader, retention, deletion, and cryptographic key lifecycle approved without arbitrary legal periods.
requirements.next_action: Obtain privacy/security decisions before persisting operational receipts or history.

requirements.description: Validate snapshot structural safety while keeping the test's actual coverage boundary explicit.
requirements.blocker: The six offline tests do not establish snapshot atomicity, source-revision consistency, reader pinning, publication correctness, or learner-state preservation.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: The complete snapshot unit file collects and passes in the isolated C14 environment; uncovered publication/restore invariants remain separate gates.
requirements.next_action: Add publication/restore concurrency and learner-state tests only in a separately authorized technical phase.

requirements.description: Approve the effect of deletes, restores, reimports, and publication on learner progress, attempts, and pinned generations.
requirements.blocker: Track/node cascades touch learner state; generation and emergency withdrawal policy must be reconciled with preserved attempts.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Policy preserves valid session generation and attempts, supports audited corrections and explicit emergency withdrawal, and forbids accidental negative credential revocation.
requirements.next_action: Approve delete/restore/withdrawal semantics before including these writers in any wave.

requirements.description: Select a first operational writer wave only after same-scope bypasses and required governance are closed.
requirements.blocker: No candidate can be safely cut over with the current decisions, runtime evidence, and overlapping legacy writers.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: A bounded writer scope has complete authority, API, privacy, same-collection coverage, tests, operational baseline, and rollback evidence.
requirements.next_action: Do not implement a writer wave; close owner decisions and operational evidence first.

requirements.description: Define a rollback that pauses entry, contains legacy writers, reconciles confirmed operations, and preserves history.
requirements.blocker: Operational pause, writer containment, receipt reconciliation, and restore path cannot be rehearsed without an approved target baseline.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: A rehearsal proves rollback does not erase committed audit/revision, reopen revoked access, duplicate intents, or enable stale writers.
requirements.next_action: Keep rollback as design only until a target and rehearsal are separately authorized.

requirements.description: Obtain the operational baseline required by ADR-008 through its authorized evidence process.
requirements.blocker: The deployed SHA/digest, route, readiness, provenance, transaction topology, roles, and integration line remain unverified; ADR-008 is blocked.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Authorized evidence identifies the actual target code and image, schema, driver, topology, roles, routing, and readiness for the intended integration line.
requirements.next_action: Request evidence via the pre-approved administrator process; C14 performs no infrastructure discovery.

requirements.description: Obtain explicit authorization for a specific implementation increment after the readiness criteria are met.
requirements.blocker: C14 authorizes consolidation only and expressly excludes runtime changes.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: A new authorization identifies branch/base, exact writers, files, environment, tests, rollback, and prohibited actions.
requirements.next_action: Submit the readiness package for owner review; no runtime work is started by this phase.

writer_coverage.scope_note: Static versioned-code coverage only; external jobs, operator tools, deployment selection, and runtime invocation remain unknown.
writer_coverage.adjacent_scope_note: These modules write learner progress, attempts, notes, reviews, or learning events; deletion/publication writers must preserve their state, but the modules do not add editorial content writers to W-01..W-17.
